card.title: Nobo Finance, Stablecoin-Powered Banking
card.subtitle: A working demo that shows how stablecoin rails can make UK–Nigeria money transfers feel like an ordinary bank transfer.

hero.title: Nobo Finance, Stablecoin-Powered Banking
hero.summary: A mobile banking app combining fiat and crypto, using stablecoins behind the scenes to make UK–Nigeria transfers faster and simpler.

blocks.html: Nobo uses stablecoins to reduce the cost and settlement time of UK–Nigeria transfers. The challenge was making those benefits accessible to mainstream users who may associate crypto with complexity and risk.
The experience balances two user needs: familiar banking with stablecoin mechanics in the background, and direct crypto controls for users who want more visibility.

I designed the end-to-end prototype across banking, cards, crypto, and cross-border transfers using Railsr's sandbox environment and simulated crypto transactions. The client used it to demonstrate the product to investors and prospective partners ahead of live infrastructure development.

blocks.title: Business Objectives
items: Demonstrate the value of stablecoin-powered UK–Nigeria transfers
Build a credible prototype for investor and partner conversations
Validate the product direction with mainstream, non-crypto users

blocks.title: Early signals being tracked
items: Buy, sell, and convert task completion
Errors or hesitation during review and confirmation

items.challenge: Doesn’t understand stablecoins, and crypto feels risky
Wants visibility and control over how money moves

blocks.html: The core tension was making a technology most users don't understand (and don't need to) feel trustworthy anyway. Traditional remittance is slow, expensive, and opaque about fees and timing; stablecoins solve that, but only if the benefit can be communicated without requiring the user to first learn what a stablecoin is.
Insights came from stakeholder interviews and demo run-throughs with the client's sales and fundraising team.

items.finding: Stablecoin-powered FX transfers felt too complex and risky for some users.
items.insight: Hide stablecoin complexity while making the benefits of lower fees, better rates, and clear recipient amounts visible.

items.finding: Crypto-curious users wanted more visibility and control over how their money moves.
items.insight: Create a separate crypto experience where users can buy, hold, convert, and send stablecoins directly.

items.finding: Unclear fees and exchange rates reduced trust in competitor apps.
items.insight: Standardise the review step to clearly show fees, exchange rates, and the amount the recipient receives.

blocks.html: Users can manage multiple accounts, top up through Open Banking, send money, and control their card and spending limits from one place. The experience follows familiar banking patterns, while stablecoin infrastructure stays behind the scenes when it is used for cross-border transfers.

Users who want more control can access their crypto holdings, individual wallets, and transaction history in one place. They can also send stablecoins directly to contacts without adding complexity to the main banking experience.

Users can buy stablecoins from their fiat account, sell them back to fiat, or convert between assets. Clear amounts, exchange rates, and fees before confirmation make each transaction easier to understand.

As this was a demo application built for fundraising and partner demonstrations, there are no live adoption or transaction metrics to report. Instead, success was measured through moderated usability testing of the prototype:

The finished prototype was used by the client in investor and partner demonstrations, helping communicate the value of stablecoin-powered transfers and align stakeholders on the product direction ahead of MVP development.

The biggest design challenge wasn't designing crypto features, it was making them disappear. Most users don't care what a stablecoin is, they care that their money arrives quickly, securely, and at a lower cost. The Basic flow was designed to feel like a familiar banking experience, while the Advanced flow gave experienced users the visibility and control they expected.

If I revisited this project, I'd explore subtle ways to reinforce the benefits of the underlying technology, such as speed, security, and transparency, without exposing its complexity. That would help users understand the value behind the experience while keeping the transfer flow simple and familiar.
